subject.title: Discord account-to-agent routing falls back to default agent instead of matching by account name

question: Should Discord multi-account routing add a guarded same-name accountId-to-agent fallback when no explicit binding matches, or should explicit bindings remain the only supported contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but changing fallback semantics affects session, auth/provider, and permission boundaries, and OpenClaw policy treats fallback behavior as a product/security decision.

options.title: Approve guarded fallback
options.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct matchedBy diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

options.title: Keep explicit bindings only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and add clearer docs, doctor, or status warnings for Discord accounts that appear intended to bind to same-named agents.

options.title: Repair replacement PR first
options.body: Use the open external fork PR only as source material after resolving conflicts, adding the missing configured-agent guard, and supplying real Discord proof.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded fallback
recommendation.body: Route non-default Discord accountIds to an existing same-named configured agent only after explicit binding tiers miss, with distinct matchedBy diagnostics, docs, tests, and live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal for multi-agent routing and repeated follow-up work on the shared resolver path.
